title: The batch that lost a shard
blurb: A crashed worker lost its shard and the batch still reported success.
prompt: A worker died mid-shard, the batch completed with 999 of 1000 shards, and the dashboard still said success because the shard was popped without a lease. The model-generated draft also counts a shard as done before flushing its output. Review it, fix it, and prove lost shards are reclaimed and honesty is enforced in the status.
aiNote: The draft pops shards with no lease, so a worker crash loses a shard from every set, and it publishes the completion event before flushing the output object, so the checksum can reference an unreadable file.
testIdea: Kill a worker mid-shard and assert the shard is reclaimed by another worker; assert a batch with any non-terminal shard never reports success; assert the checksum of a published shard matches the flushed object.
followUps: What retry semantics should a shard have when its worker dies after a partial write?
How would you make one million model calls cost-aware?
What does the manifest need so a downstream consumer can trust a batch?
